title: Testard's particular grace: salvation effectually applied to the elect
source_text: XXXI. Per gratiam vero particularem intelligit illam qua Deus certos ex hominibus revera salutis participes efficit, Christi beneficium illis non simpliciter offerendo, sed efficaciter & reapse applicando. Vocat autem gratiam illam particularem, quoniam non ut prior ad omnes extenditur, sed est paucorum propria, electorum, scilicet, ut quae consistat in ipsa electione, & beneficiis inde promanantibus: qualia sunt vocatio interna & efficax, justificatio, perseverantiae donum & glorificatio.
pass_a_gloss: XXXI. But by particular grace he understands that by which God makes certain of men truly partakers of salvation, not simply offering the benefit of Christ to them, but efficaciously and actually applying it. And he calls that grace particular, because it is not extended to all as the former, but is proper to few, namely the elect, as that which consists in election itself, and the benefits flowing from it: such as are internal and efficacious calling, justification, the gift of perseverance and glorification.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXI. By particular grace he means the grace by which God makes certain people actually share in salvation, not merely offering them Christ's benefit but applying it to them effectually and in fact.

He calls this grace particular because, unlike the first, it does not reach everyone but belongs to a few, namely the elect, since it consists in election itself and in the benefits that flow from it: internal and effectual calling, justification, the gift of perseverance and glorification.
